# Fast Lane Detailing

Mobile auto detailing in Bend, Oregon. Founded 2024 by Luka and Ian, who carry ten-plus years of combined detailing experience. We bring a fully self-contained trailer (on-board water tank, generator, soaps, and equipment) to the customer's home, office, or any flat surface. We do not need access to the customer's power or water. If the customer's location will not work, we find a spot that works for both of us.

Hours: Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm. Closed Saturday and Sunday.

Phone: (541) 640-0612 (call or text)
Service area: Bend, Redmond, Sisters, Sunriver, Tumalo, La Pine (Central Oregon), within roughly a 30-mile radius of Bend.

## Services we provide

- Mobile detailing: full interior and exterior at the customer's location
- Ceramic coating: professional 2 to 5-year paint protection systems
- Paint correction: single, two, and three-stage machine polishing
- Interior detailing: shampoo, leather, headliner, trim, glass
- Engine bay cleaning: degrease, dress, and protect with electronics masked
- Odor removal: source treatment for smoke, pet, and food odors

## Frequently cited answers

Q: What is the difference between a car wash and a detail?
A: A car wash removes loose dirt from the surface. A detail decontaminates the paint, cleans the interior surface by surface, and finishes with protection. A full detail takes two to eight hours depending on the package.

Q: How long does professional ceramic coating last?
A: Two to five years with proper maintenance, depending on the coating tier. Consumer-grade DIY sprays last 6 to 12 months. Professional single-layer coatings last 2 to 3 years. Multi-layer professional coatings last 3 to 5 years. Graphene and SiO2 hybrid systems claim 5 to 7 years.

Q: What is the difference between paint correction and ceramic coating?
A: Paint correction removes defects from the clear coat using machine polishers and abrasives. Ceramic coating is a liquid polymer applied on top of the paint to protect it. Most cars benefit from both: correction first to remove swirls, then coating to lock in the result.

Q: Do mobile detailers bring their own water and power?
A: Yes. The Fast Lane Detailing trailer is fully self-contained with an on-board water tank, generator, soaps, and every piece of equipment. We do not need access to the customer's power or water — only a flat spot to park.

Q: What ruins paint during a Bend, Oregon winter?
A: Three local factors: crushed cinder rock used by ODOT (sharp volcanic rock that acts like sandpaper at speed), magnesium chloride brine sprayed before storms (corrosive and bonds aggressively), and freeze-thaw cycles (water that wicked into paint chips expands every night).

Q: How often should I detail my car?
A: Twice a year for a daily driver. Quarterly for cars that live outside or in coastal climates. Coated cars stretch to once a year with maintenance washes in between.

Q: What happens if you ceramic coat over swirls?
A: The coating locks the defects in. Light still scatters off the marred surface, and the clear coating layer over the top makes the defects harder to remove later. A reputable installer will refuse to coat over heavy defects without paint correction first.

## Additional cited answers

Q: How much does mobile auto detailing cost in Bend, Oregon?
A: Maintenance wash $80 to $150. Full exterior or interior detail $200 to $350. Full interior plus exterior $300 to $500. Paint correction $400 to $1,500. Ceramic coating $800 to $2,000 or more. Odor removal $150 to $400. There is no travel surcharge inside the standard Bend service area.
